    Dragons¶

    An ancient, spaceborn species — one of the few races on Ge'or whose origins lie beyond the Glorious Alliance survivors. Dragons once ruled the world during the Dragon Tyranny (6,999–5,500 BGD), when twelve clans controlled ninety percent of the known land. Today they are nearly extinct: wild dragons roam remote wilderness, and the last civilized population lives in the frozen highlands of Kramsadar.

    Biology¶

    • Origin: Spaceborn — dragons evolved in space, where their hoarding instinct began as a survival drive: attracting metallic asteroids for shelter from radiation
    • Lifespan: Millennia. Civilized dragons speak with the weight of millennia — a dragon in full form is indistinguishable from a god to most species
    • Forms: Dragons possess a full form and lesser forms; most of the world encounters them only in their smaller incarnations
    • Types: Wild dragons — territorial predators driven by instinct, hoarding treasure out of an inherited drive. Civilized dragons — fully sapient, capable of language, culture, and society
    • Mage-cell expression: Extreme in civilized bloodlines — dragon magic is the largest concentration of power on Ge'or, as proven by The Draconic War, whose discharge saturated the atmosphere with the Black Agent

    Society¶

    Civilized dragon society is honor-based, ascetic, and deliberately removed from the world.

    • Nation: Kramsadar on Marti Continent — the last significant population of civilized dragons. Half tundra, half near-permafrost, chosen deliberately: the dragons want to be left alone
    • Culture: Honor codes, personal oaths, and ritualized combat. They do not meddle in Ge'orian affairs — they follow Daicrodism, worship their god, conduct ancient rituals, and live peaceful, contemplative lives
    • Religion: Daicrodism — the atonement faith of peace and prosperity for all beings, evolved from the war-religion Diocronism after the death wars. The seclusion of Kramsadar is itself an act of faith. The exception: rogue dragons — the uncivilized ones — follow no faith.
    • History: Twelve clans ruled ninety percent of the world in Age 4; their empire collapsed in the death wars. The dragon empires of Klobiendar and Xi fell in The Draconic War, leaving Dragonreach haunted by Fallen Dragons
    • Notable: Goldenborn — the Dragon-King of Baoth, now in quasi-death; Dragon Yaldabaoth — the entity inhabiting the Ruins of Baoth

    Dragon Types¶

    Wild Dragons¶

    Wild dragons are beasts — territorial, predatory, and driven by instinct. They are the rogue exception: uncivilized, they follow no faith, unlike the Daicrodism-keeping civilized dragons. They lair in remote mountains, deep forests, or volcanic caverns. They hoard treasure not out of greed but out of an instinctive drive to accumulate — a behavior left over from their spaceborne evolution, when attracting metallic asteroids provided shelter from radiation. Wild dragons can be hunted — though the hunters rarely return.

    Civilized Dragons¶

    Civilized dragons are fully sapient, capable of language, culture, and society. The dragons of Kramsadar on Marti Continent are the last significant population of civilized dragons on Ge'or. They are:

    • Honor-based — their society is built on codes of conduct, personal oaths, and ritualized combat.
    • Deity-like — those who encounter civilized dragons often describe them in religious terms. A dragon in full form, speaking with the weight of millennia, is indistinguishable from a god to most species.
    • Ascetic — they do not meddle in Ge'orian affairs. They have better things to do: worship their god, conduct ancient rituals, and live peaceful, contemplative lives.
    • Isolated — Kramsadar is half tundra, half near-permafrost. The dragons chose this place deliberately. They want to be left alone.

    Notable Dragons¶

    • Goldenborn — The Dragon-King of Baoth, now in quasi-death
    • Dragon Yaldabaoth — The entity inhabiting the Ruins of Baoth
